picks.file: Venedig, Vedute Erhard Reuwichs in Peregrinationes in terram sanctam, Mainz 1486.jpg
picks.what: Woodcut panorama in Bernhard von Breydenbach, Peregrinatio in terram sanctam
picks.why: original first printed view of Venice (the model for the Nuremberg Chronicle view); focal on the Civitas Venetiarum banner, Campanile and Doge’s Palace

picks.file: 1636 bird's eye view of Venice by Matthäus Merian.jpg
picks.why: high-resolution colored bird’s-eye view, San Marco and the Grand Canal clear

picks.file: L'Altea Parte della Piazza S. Marco Di Venetia.jpg
picks.what: The Piazza San Marco, engraving in Merian’s Topographia Italiae
picks.why: hand-colored view of the basilica, Campanile and Procuratie; margins trimmed

picks.file: Giuseppe Bernardino Bison Piazza San Marco.jpg
picks.what: The Piazzetta with the Doge’s Palace and the Campanile, painting
picks.why: color view of the Piazzetta: St. Mark’s column, Campanile, clock tower and Doge’s Palace
color Grand Canal scene with palazzi and a gondola

picks.file: Gezicht op Venetië vanaf het schip Esperia met links de kerk S Maria della Salu, Bestanddeelnr 254-2014.jpg
picks.what: Santa Maria della Salute and the Campanile from the water, photograph (Nationaal Archief)
picks.why: the Salute dome, Dogana and Campanile across the Giudecca Canal

picks.file: Backplate – Venice Dawn 2 (Greg Zaal and Rico Cilliers via Poly Haven) DSC07252.jpg
picks.what: The Doge’s Palace and the Riva degli Schiavoni at dawn, photograph
picks.why: sharp modern view of the Doge’s Palace; no skyline photo among candidates

notes: P0: chose Reuwich’s original 1486 print over the Nuremberg Chronicle view, since #1–#3 are scans of a 1930 facsimile reprint. Merian’s Venice plate is dated 1636 on Commons (sources vary 1635–40). Skipped: #16 (Canaletto attribution and date only presumptive, photo of framed painting), #15 (1704 reissue of the Merian bird’s-eye design), #21 (Guardi drawing includes the unbuilt Teatro Manin project), #31 (poster of the London ‘Venice’ show), #37 (costume genre scene), #42 (a painting of Tivoli). P4 alternative: Melan’s 1854 Doge’s Palace painting (#28), close to Bison’s 1844 subject.
